known_final_diagnosis: Analysis of pleural fluid showed elevated triglycerides of 319 mg/dL consistent with chylothorax. Flow cytometry of the pleural fluid showed that 3% of total cells were monotypic B cells, expressing CD19, CD20, CD45 and kappa light chain but were negative for CD5 and CD10. The T cells (36% of total cells) showed a CD4:CD8 ratio of 4.8:1, with normal expression of CD5. Cytology of fluid revealed moderately cellular effusion with abundant small lymphocytes mixed with a few reactive mesothelial cells. Findings were consistent with B-cell lymphoma.

report.source_text: Following thoracentesis, she had slight improvement in her shortness of breath. She was also started on a fat-free diet. However, she developed re-accumulation of pleural fluid several days later and required second thoracentesis with pigtail catheter placement. Repeat fluid analysis showed decreasing triglycerides to 94 mg/dL and negative cultures. She was discharged in stable condition; pigtail catheter was removed prior to discharge.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 50-year-old woman with a history of Waldenstrom’s macroglobulinaemia presented with right-sided pleuritic chest pain and progressive dyspnoea. A chest X-ray revealed a right pleural effusion. Thoracentesis and subsequent pleural fluid analysis confirmed elevated triglycerides (319 mg/dL) consistent with chylothorax, and flow cytometry identified monotypic B cells (CD19, CD20, CD45, kappa light chain positive) and abundant small lymphocytes, consistent with B-cell lymphoma. The patient experienced re-accumulation of pleural fluid, requiring a second thoracentesis with pigtail catheter placement. A subsequent bone marrow biopsy confirmed extensive infiltration by B-cell lymphoma. She was treated with ibrutinib, leading to the resolution of her pleural effusion within 2 months.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with right-sided pleuritic chest pain and progressive dyspnoea, with a known history of Waldenstrom’s macroglobulinaemia.
Initial chest X-ray demonstrated a right pleural effusion.
Pleural fluid analysis showed elevated triglycerides of 319 mg/dL, consistent with chylothorax.
Flow cytometry of the pleural fluid showed 3% monotypic B cells (CD19, CD20, CD45, kappa light chain positive; CD5, CD10 negative), consistent with B-cell lymphoma.
Cytology of pleural fluid revealed moderately cellular effusion with abundant small lymphocytes.
Patient required a second thoracentesis with pigtail catheter placement due to re-accumulation of pleural fluid, with repeat fluid analysis showing decreasing triglycerides.

Repeat bone marrow biopsy demonstrated hypercellular marrow with 90% infiltrate of small-to-intermediate lymphocytes and plasma cells, and flow cytometry confirmed extensive infiltration by B-cell lymphoma.
Patient was started on ibrutinib, and her pleural effusion resolved within 2 months.

remaining_uncertainties: Long-term follow-up and prognosis beyond the 2-month resolution of pleural effusion are not documented.
